name: Copper Verdigris
replaces: Isomer core palette (Isomer Blue, Accent Purple, Secondary Orange)
summary: Copper signals. Verdigris acts. Black, white and gray carry the page. Outside the work, copper and verdigris are the brand.

semantics.copper: In the work: risk found, flagged, rising, warning, too late. In a brand moment: the metal, the larger share of every device.
semantics.verdigris: In the work: action, whoever takes it. Isomer acting in a figure; what the reader can do in a product (links, selection, focus, controls, advice). In a brand moment: a trace of patina at the end of a device, never the field.
semantics.oxide-red: critical or irreversible (status only, always with its word)
semantics.cobalt: OK, healthy, info (status only, always with its word)
semantics.graphite: screens of data, and the dark product theme
semantics.neutrals: every frame: rules, panels, tabs, chart bars, numbers, dates, labels, the ruler

typography.note: Titles, headlines and display values are Fustat, the Isomer brand face. Body text, UI and captions are Inter. IBM Plex Mono is for labels and counts only.

families.title: Neutrals
families.description: About 85% of any surface. Graphite has a trace of green so it sits with the verdigris.

colors.name: Graphite
colors.use: Product screens, and the dark theme's surfaces

colors.name: Graphite deep
colors.use: Dark theme ground; pressed states on screens

colors.name: Graphite raised
colors.use: Rules and raised rows on graphite

colors.name: On-graphite muted
colors.use: Secondary text on graphite. Never on white (2.4:1)

colors.name: Body
colors.use: Running and secondary text, in product and email

colors.name: Muted
colors.use: Meta only: dates, sources, captions, footers. Never running text; 10px minimum

colors.name: Rule
colors.use: Panel borders in product and email; a step firmer than hairline so it holds on white

families.title: Copper · the signal
families.description: In the work: risk flags, HIGH tags, "too late", rising. Doubles as the warning color. As brand: the metal in the mark, a cover, one hero word. Never on eyebrows, labels or numbers that aren't risky. Never a full-bleed background.

colors.name: Copper
colors.use: Risk marks, too-late dots, the 8px 'why it matters' square

colors.name: Copper deep
colors.use: Brand devices on paper (the bar, the band), one hero word. Not eyebrows or labels

colors.name: Copper dark
colors.use: Risk text and labels on light grounds (6.8:1 on white)

colors.name: Copper light
colors.use: Risk on graphite and in the dark theme; brand devices on ink

families.title: Verdigris · the action
families.description: In the work: action, whoever takes it. ACT pills, the X-ray scan line and Isomer outcomes in figures; links, selection, controls and focus in a product. As brand: a trace of patina at the end of a device, never a field.

colors.name: Verdigris
colors.use: Action marks, ACT pills, the 8px 'what you can do' square. Not text on white (4.0:1)

colors.name: Verdigris deep
colors.use: Links, selected state, focus rings, action text on light (6.1:1 on white); the patina trace in devices on paper

colors.name: Verdigris light
colors.use: Action on graphite and in the dark theme; scan line on screens; the patina trace in devices on ink

families.title: Status · for apps
families.description: Three states, not four. Warning reuses copper. Red is reserved for critical or broken. Cobalt means healthy and doubles as info. Always pair status color with a label or icon.

distinctiveness: Copper and verdigris carry the identity through a small set of brand devices on ink or paper (the oxidation band, the short oxidation bar, the bar and pixel), and carry meaning everywhere else. Never both jobs on one surface.
Carry the plate apparatus (rulers, plate codes, scan line) into page UI in gray, low opacity. Copper ticks on a ruler are decoration.
Avoid category-default patterns: big-number tiles over a mono caption row, dark 'extraction' text blocks, numbered section eyebrows, red/green status dots without a word.
Make time the subject: show when something was caught, not just what a file contains.

brand.what: Copper and verdigris as identity: the patina story, copper becoming verdigris, told by a few flat devices on an ink or paper ground.

dark.use: Covers, title and closing slides, social cards, event

light.use: Section slides, documents and reports, anything with a lot of reading

logo.rule: Use the black (ink) and white logos with this palette. The current color logos are drawn in the old blue and purple and don't belong on Copper Verdigris surfaces.
notes: Every file has a transparent background; the paper and ink behind them on the logo board are only the preview. The white files can look blank in a file preview or on a light page because they are white on transparent. Place them on ink or graphite.
The logo is not a device: it doesn't count toward one colored device per view, and it never takes copper or verdigris.
The ink files are the solid-dark logos recolored from Isomer Blue #000441 to ink #141416; shapes are unchanged. The white files are the solid-light logos.
Product screens use the logo in the heading color: ink on light, white on dark.

devices.name: Oxidation band
devices.form: A full-width flat strip on the bottom (or top) edge: 70% copper, 20% the second copper, 10% verdigris, copper first
devices.size: About 1.5 to 3% of the width: 32px on a 1920 slide, 16px on a 1200 social card
devices.use: Covers, title and closing slides, social cards, the site footer, event and print

devices.name: Short oxidation bar
devices.form: The band at mark size, same proportions
devices.size: About 2.5x the headline size wide and 0.18x tall: 84 x 6 under a 34px headline, 160 x 12 under a 64px one
devices.use: The everyday signature: under a section-slide or document headline, beside the logo, in an email or document masthead

devices.name: Bar and pixel
devices.form: A copper bar and one verdigris square, its side equal to the bar's height, one bar-height apart
devices.size: Bar about 1.6x the headline size wide; 56 x 6 plus 6 x 6 under a 34px headline
devices.use: The quietest form: small sizes, slide footers, email signatures, the app icon

devices.name: Ruler
devices.form: Gray ticks along the top edge, minor every 8px, major every 40px, about 70% opacity. No color
devices.size: 8px tall on a card, 16px on a slide
devices.use: Adds the instrument look to any ground; combine with any colored device

devices.name: Ruler and band
devices.form: The ruler on top and the oxidation band at the base: the page framed like an instrument plate
devices.use: The fullest expression. Covers and title slides only

where: Covers: decks, reports, blog headers, social cards
Mastheads and footers of the site, documents and email
rules: Choose the device by context; they are one system, used with discretion, not one mark repeated everywhere.
One colored device per view. The ruler is neutral and doesn't count.
Devices sit in the frame (cover, masthead, footer, slide edge), never inside content and never touching data.
Ink or paper is the field. Verdigris is never the field and never more than the patina trace.
Keep the band's order and proportions: copper first, about 70 / 20 / 10. Flat segments, no gradients, no reversal.
On ink use copper light and verdigris light; on paper use copper deep and verdigris deep.
Dark for covers, title and closing slides; light for section slides, documents and reading.
Product screens carry no devices. The logo is enough.

signal.what: Copper and verdigris as verbs, inside the work: figures, product screens, email, charts, tables.
where: Any page section that shows data or claims
rules: Copper appears only where something is risky. If nothing on the screen is, the screen has no copper.
Verdigris appears only where something is being done, or can be.
Everything else is ink and gray: rules, panels, tabs, numbers, eyebrows, the ruler.
One meaning per color, one color per element.
